title: Biscuits and Gravy
shortDescription: Southern comfort for a slow morning
subtitle: Southern comfort for a slow morning
description: Southern comfort for a slow morning. Sized for a full crew, with timing that still works when the kitchen gets interrupted.

steps.title: Bake the biscuits
steps.instruction: Bake biscuits at 425°F per mix directions until tall and golden — 14–18 minutes. Split and hold in a towel while gravy finishes.

steps.title: Brown the sausage
steps.instruction: Crumble sausage in a large skillet over medium-high until no pink remains. Leave the fat — that's the gravy body.

steps.title: Make the pepper gravy
steps.instruction: Sprinkle flour over sausage; stir 1 minute. Whisk in milk gradually. Simmer 5–8 minutes until thick enough to coat a spoon. Season with plenty of black pepper.

steps.title: Split and smother
steps.instruction: Split biscuits on sheet trays. Ladle hot gravy over the line. Hold gravy in a warm pot on low — stir before each ladle so it doesn't skin over.

proTips: Keep a backup tray warm in the oven for late calls — nothing worse than cold plates after a run.
Taste for salt at the end — hall palates run salty after long shifts.
tonightSpread: Plate Biscuits and Gravy with sides in separate pans so the crew can mix portions.
Keep hot items on one side of the table and cold on the other — eggs stay hot, fruit stays cold.
Line up Biscuits and Gravy on the main counter with serving spoons — firefighters grab fast between calls.
Keep a backup tray warm in the oven at 200°F for late arrivals after a run.
leftovers: Cool leftovers in shallow containers within two hours — deep pots stay hot too long.
Label trays with date and reheat to 165°F minimum before second shift.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Southern comfort for a slow morning. A hall pick for regular dinner nights — one line, real portions, no drama at the stove.
